game: CHI @ MIN Week 11 2025, kickoff 2025-11-16 13:00 ET, US Bank Stadium dome

script.base: Closing line is MIN -3, total 47.5, implied MIN 25.2 / CHI 22.2 in a dome, so the book has a close game with Minnesota up by about a score, not a blowout and not a slog. Chicago's weeks 8-10 offense has been run-leaning (Monangai 40/228, Swift 24/125, Williams 14/142) while Minnesota funnels throws to Jefferson (32 targets, 158 yards, 351 air). Both quarterbacks stay in; the late lean is a mild Minnesota clock run, split between Jones (23/140) and Mason (18/64).
script.flip1: Minnesota jumps up by two scores early, runs the clock with Jones/Mason, and Chicago abandons the run so Monangai's carries die and Williams' air yards move to Odunze (23 targets, 325 air in weeks 8-10), Moore and Loveland.
script.flip2: Chicago's run game controls and keeps it within a score or leads, Monangai stays on the field, and Minnesota has to throw more to Jefferson/Addison/Nailor to catch up. Spread is only 3, so the 3.5+ underdog-must-throw rule does not fully trigger.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report, not the 90-minute inactives (those are not in the pack). CHI LB T.J. Edwards Out (hand) softens the second level for MIN RBs and TEs. CHI WR Jahdae Walker Out (concussion) is a depth receiver, so targets stay with Odunze, Moore, Zaccheaus and Loveland. CHI CB Jaylon Johnson (groin) and S Jaquan Brisker (back) are Questionable only, so Jefferson/Addison/Nailor are not priced as facing confirmed backups. MIN C Ryan Kelly Out (concussion) is an interior-line downgrade: rush efficiency down, more quick throws, which hurts Jones/Mason yards and can help Jones/Hockenson catches. MIN LB Jonathan Greenard Out (shoulder) removes an edge rusher, which helps Chicago protection and the run game more than it creates a skill-position sleeper.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack, so shell is unknown. MIN YPA allowed: left 7.05 (96 att), middle 10.65 (63), right 5.87 (92). CHI YPA allowed: left 7.85 (102), middle 9.38 (65), right 7.91 (109).
matchup.pressure: MIN blitzes 50%; CHI EPA/db is +0.25 vs blitz and +0.10 vs no blitz, so Minnesota pressure does not suppress Chicago. CHI blitzes only 31%; MIN EPA/db is -0.26 vs blitz and -0.04 vs no blitz, so McCarthy is worse when blitzed but Chicago does not live there. Greenard Out further lowers MIN pressure.
matchup.bleeds: MIN bleed is the middle (10.65 YPA), not the right side; rush defense is ordinary (4.31 YPC, 32 runs of 10+, 21 passes of 20+ for 275 yards). CHI bleeds the middle and both edges and allows explosives (5.24 YPC, 36 runs of 10+, 36 passes of 20+ for 297 yards).
matchup.overlap: The clean schematic overlap is Jefferson (32 targets, 351 air in weeks 8-10) into Chicago's middle/explosive leak, but his yards are falling (L3 158; the three last4 figures that sum to that are 74, 47, 37) and Johnson/Brisker are only questionable, so that overlap is not a bet. Chicago's run volume is a usage overlap against a MIN front that is not a wall (4.31 YPC), not a soft-front overlap. Odunze (23 targets, 325 air, L3 200 yards) vs the MIN middle is real, but the line is 62.5 and the recent cluster 114, 0, 86 includes a zero.

form: Pack last4 figures are used only where three of them sum to the weeks 8-10 yard total, treated as the recent cluster. Monangai rush last4 81, 24, 176, 28 and 24+176+28=228, so the recent cluster is 24, 176, 28 against a 24.5 line (one miss by half a yard). Mason rush last4 57, 3, 36, 25 and 3+36+25=64, so the recent cluster is 3, 36, 25, all under 52.5, after an older 57. Jones rush recent cluster 15, 78, 47 (L3 140 on 23 carries) vs a 23.5 line. Jefferson recent cluster 74, 47, 37 (L3 158 on 32 targets) vs 75.5. Addison recent cluster 26, 48, 35 vs 44.5. Nailor recent cluster 0, 16, 124, one-play inflated. Hockenson recent cluster 26, 11, 8 vs 26.5. Odunze recent cluster 114, 0, 86. Moore recent cluster 73, 72, 0. Zaccheaus recent cluster 33, 58, 5. Swift last4 rush 108, 124, 45, 80 does not reconcile to L3 125, so he is not used.

Johnson and Brisker are Questionable, not Out, so they are not sleeper triggers.

edge_players.must_be_true: He keeps about 8+ carries, Swift (24 carries, 125 yards in that same window) does not take the job back, and Chicago is not down multiple scores early.
edge_players.kills_it: A repeat of the 24-yard game in the recent cluster, or Minnesota getting up big so Chicago abandons the run.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because the 176-yard Monangai game was the fluke, Minnesota's 4.31 YPC front held him to another 24-yard day after Chicago fell behind and Swift took the designed runs, while Edwards being out and Chicago allowing 5.24 YPC let Mason grind as the closer in a Minnesota lead and clear 52.5 on one explosive the way the older 57-yard game did. That counter is real on Mason and is why the card is flagged; it is not stronger than a 6-carry role against a 52.5 number, and it is weaker than Monangai's usage gap.
slip_story: One close-game carry-split story, not a shootout and not a blowout stack: trust weeks 8-10 roles in a dome MIN -3 / 47.5 game. Monangai over and Mason under can win together if Chicago still runs and Minnesota keeps splitting carries. Do not add Jefferson, Odunze or Nailor overs to this slip; those need the pass-heavy flip. No TD legs. Two legs only because no third prop cleared the read.
